paras: Tropidophis morenoi, also commonly known as the zebra dwarf boa and the zebra trope, is a species of snake in the family Tropidophiidae. The species is endemic to Cuba.
The specific name, morenoi, is in honor of Cuban herpetologist Luis V. Moreno.
Tropidophis morenoi is found in north-central Cuba, in the provinces of Ciego de Ávila, Sancti Spíritus, and Villa Clara.
The preferred natural habitat of Tropidophis morenoi is forest, at altitudes from sea level to 25 m (82 ft).

Tropidophis morenoi is distinguished from other Tropidophis species by its buff ground color, with  brown spots fused to form zebra-like bands. The longest specimen measured is a female with a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 35.9 cm (14.1 in) and a tail length of 5.7 cm (2.2 in).
